items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: So I went with Don, and I had a great experience with Don. That was great to work with him, because he was another giant.

ctx.x: I left... See, I made up my band... My wife was pregnant. And I had just had the road, and I had this aspiration to teach. So I took it all the way out there. Teachers stay in town. So I told you the story. I went to him and said, "Fess, I've got to give my notice." He said, "You can't do that." I already had my gig. I already had my job with Don Redman.

So I went with Don, and I had a great experience with Don. That was great to work with him, because he was another giant. He could write, boy. Don Redman didn't care nothin' about the key of D and the key of E. It was just as easy to him as the key of C. And he wrote. And he could play, too. See, he played lead on all his arrangements. And he was a beautiful guy. I got close to him. I used to hang out with him when the gig was over. I'd go uptown with him...
I've got some pictures of you and Tyree and him together.
